title: The entry-candidate contract: the resource and parameter names, the response entity, its field names, the paging, the error status set and the access rule are not fixed by any source, and this legacy key has no contract story of its own
source: Legacy RWB-E1-018 sections 4, 12 and 13; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14, A2.15 and T-A.1; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.4, T6.2, T6.3 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 15, 29 and 41; split plan slices of RWB-E1-018; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths X5 and X6; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10 Authority; 12.1; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: Six elements of the one operation this slice delivers are absent from every source. (1) No source names an entry-candidate resource: the legacy read was the in-process AceSourceQuery interface with accountsAtOrAbove(daysPastDue, businessDate), relationsFor(accountKey) and customer(personKey), and the target API inventory of P1 lists no operation that returns accounts at or above a threshold for a business date. (2) The names of the two query parameters, their bounds and whether the threshold may be omitted are not stated; the legacy threshold was the parameter case.entry.dpd of rwb-case. (3) The response entity, its element names and the element names of a candidate row are not stated; the legacy AccountEntrySnapshot carried accountKey, accountCode, productGroup, regionCode, daysPastDue, totalBalance, tdrFlag and dataAsOf and no exclusion fact, while the exclusion facts of this slice are five more fields from three owners. (4) Paging is not stated, although the FSD counts about 28,100 accounts at 90 days past due or more at go-live (DL15). (5) The error status set is not stated: the legacy read threw Java exceptions and had no status code, and no source fixes the status of an incomplete ALS batch, a missing parameter or a view failure. (6) The access rule of the read and of the two extension writes is not stated: the legacy read ran as the JOB-02 service identity and the legacy extension rows were written by CaseAndWorkflowRepository of the monolith, so neither a caller identity nor a right exists for the target. The split plan of this legacy key lists RWB-P3-E1018-CON as the case contract and no contract story for this slice, so nothing publishes these shapes before the story is built.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 12 ('// P1, used by this story (RWB-E1-016); every method reads recovery.v_ace_*; public interface AceSourceQuery { List<AccountEntrySnapshot> accountsAtOrAbove(int daysPastDue, LocalDate businessDate); ... }' and the AccountEntrySnapshot field list) and section 13 (CaseAndWorkflowRepository 'recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, account_ext, party_ext'); TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 (API-P1-001 to API-P1-016, none of them an entry-candidate read) and T6.2 ('Each endpoint declares its capability area and right'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (P1 IN: 'REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id} - GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId= - GET /freshness (business date) - POST /business-days/{date}/ready') and slide 41 (P1 first API path /customers/{id}); FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP01 expected by 08:00) and the legacy section 6 count ('about 28,100 accounts at 90 days past due', DL15); split plan (_work/msr/plan/split_plan.json, slices of RWB-E1-018: no P1 contract story); Template and Rules v1 R5.4 (C dependency, build against the published contract and its fake) and R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13
area: Contract: entry-candidate resource, parameters, response entity, paging, errors and access
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-source-data with the solution architect and the P3 owner of the case contract
proposed: Publish one read, GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/entry-candidates with businessDate and threshold as required query parameters and page and size optional, answering EntryCandidatePage with businessDate, threshold, asOf, page, size, total, candidates[] and breaks[]; name the candidate elements after the field they read; fix the status set at 400, 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503; and let this story publish the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of the three operations with the service API document, because no contract story of this key exists. The read is called by the service identity of the rwb-case case creation step and the two extension writes by the exclusion screen through gateway-bff. Every choice is recorded in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-1.

title: Whether the entry read is one operation for a business date or one operation per account, and how a page of about 28,100 candidates is cut, are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 4 steps 4 to 6; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.4 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 15; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and R5.7
section: 4 Flow steps 5 to 8; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 12.1; 13 Solution plan build steps 4 and 6
description: The legacy job looped over the accounts it read: CaseCreationJob 'calls CaseEntryService per account_key' and each call read the relations and the customer for that one account. The target fixes two things the legacy shape does not answer. (1) It is not stated whether the target offers one call for the business date or a call per account, and the choice decides whether the case creation job takes one hop or about 28,100 hops, against the one-hop rule of DP-11. (2) No source states how a response of that size is paged, what the default and maximum page size are, or whether the caller pages through the view or receives the whole date in one response; the FSD gives no page size for P1's record reads either.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 13 ('CaseCreationJob | Job | JOB-02; listens for AceDataReady; checks the ALS batch row for the business date; calls CaseEntryService per account_key') and section 4 step 4 ('reads v_ace_account for every account with days_past_due at or above 90 and data_as_of equal to the business date'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (REST: 'Never | Call chains (depth > 1)'; '2 s; retry GET only (once, jitter); breaker + bulkhead') and slide 15 (P1 temporal activity 'listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page)', which names a page but not its size); TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 (no operation and no paging rule for an entry read); FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP01 expected by 08:00, no volume per call)
area: Read shape: one call per business date against one call per account, and paging
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-source-data with the owner of the rwb-case case creation job
proposed: One operation for the business date, executed as one statement set and paged by page and size, so the caller takes one hop; a per-account read is refused as a fan-out under DP-11. The default and maximum page size are fixed in the published contract, and the caller pages through the date. Recorded in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-2.

title: Which service writes account_ext.dispute_open and the party_ext flags, which right the confirmation needs, and where party_ext.vulnerable comes from on the first write are not settled
source: FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1 (BR-P1-001-5, AC-ALT-P1-001-03, field catalog) and A2.15; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.5; Legacy RWB-E1-018 sections 3 and 13; ownership map of the D-RCV-60 plan; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11 and 29
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow step 11; 5 Exception paths X3; 7 Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 13 Solution plan
description: The four extension tables are P1's (ownership map; TSD P1 v3 T3.5), and the FSD says an extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column, and is written when a person records the decision. What is not settled is who writes them in the target and under which right. (1) The legacy story wrote party_ext and account_ext from CaseAndWorkflowRepository in the same transaction as the case, and its screen was the case record; the target splits the case (rwb-case) from the extension tables (rwb-source-data), and no source says whether the exclusion screen calls P1 or whether P1 writes the row on a case event. (2) The confirmation is described as 'a fraud specialist confirms fraud on the case', but no role code of a fraud specialist exists in any source, and the ownership map gives the access model to rwb-access (P4); the right that authorises the write is therefore unstated. (3) party_ext.vulnerable is mandatory in TSD P1 v3 T3.5 and on the FSD field catalog, and no source says which screen sets it or what the first write puts there when the confirmation is about fraud only. (4) No source states the effect on an existing row: whether the second confirmation replaces the flags, merges them or is refused.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.1 AC-ALT-P1-001-03 ('a fraud specialist confirms fraud on the case and the Workbench writes party_ext with fraud_flag true ... public.customer for "P0000123" is unchanged And no foreign key links party_ext to public.customer'), BR-P1-001-5 ('An extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column. It is 1:1 with the ACE record and carries the seven standard record columns'), A2.1.3.2 (party_ext.vulnerable, .deceased_override, .bankruptcy and .fraud_flag are all Required Yes) and A2.15.3.2 (party_ext.vulnerable is personal data); TSD P1 v3 T3.5 ('These are 1:1 tables keyed by an ACE business key ... Their primary key is the business key: there is no id, and there is no foreign key into public'); legacy RWB-E1-018 section 13 ('CaseAndWorkflowRepository | recovery_case, case_account, case_party, case_entry_exclusion, account_ext, party_ext') and section 3 (the EXCLUSION inputs include 'account_ext.dispute_open' and 'party_ext.deceased_override, .bankruptcy and .fraud_flag'); ownership map (_work/msr/plan/ownership.json: account_ext, party_ext, contact_point_ext and valuation_ext owner P1; role, permission and masking_rule owner P4); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 11 (gateway-bff, one hop) and slide 29 (one login per service, grants enforced)
area: Extension tables: writer, right, vulnerable flag and the repeat of a confirmation
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 service owner, the P3 owner of the exclusion screen and the P4 owner of the role model
proposed: P1 writes the two rows, because only P1 holds the schema and the login, through two PUT operations by business key called by the exclusion screen through gateway-bff; the screen keeps the right, the confirmation and its audit, and P1 validates the caller's token and enforces no role model of its own. The body carries all four party flags, so vulnerable is always written by the caller and never defaulted by P1; a repeat of the same body leaves one row and a changed body replaces the flags on the same key with a version increment. Settled in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-3 and proved in AC3.

title: The ALS batch gate before RWB-ACE-001 lands: v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view, and the behaviour of an entry read for a date whose batch record does not exist yet is not specified
source: FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1 (OQ-P1-01), A2.14 (OQ-P1-02, BR-P1-014-2, BR-P1-014-4); TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.2, T3.4 and T3.7; Legacy RWB-E1-018 sections 3 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Template and Rules v1 R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 3 and 4; 5 Exception paths X4; 7 Acceptance criteria AC4; 12.8; 13 Solution plan
description: The gate of this story reads v_ace_batch_status, and that view is one of the 14 Section B views that do not exist until RWB-ACE-001 is deployed (DL43; FSD OQ-P1-01). Three things are unresolved. (1) While the view does not exist, no source says what the entry read answers: refuse every date, answer with the facts but an unknown batch, or fall back to another source. (2) The FSD records that the change register costs a freshness fallback of Tier 1 views plus the case list and 'names no freshness source for it' (OQ-P1-02), so a fallback cannot be built from a source value. (3) The status code and the wording of the refusal are not fixed; the message MSG-P1-001 exists and is worded for a product and a date, but no source says which status a client sees when the gate holds. The legacy story put the gate behind a feature flag and read the same view, which does not answer (1).
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 3 ('v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view, so the batch gate stays behind its flag until RWB-ACE-001 lands (DL43)') and section 13 ('The batch gate reads a Section B view, so the flag is on only after RWB-ACE-001 lands and V0003 creates v_ace_batch_status (DL43)'); FSD P1 v3 A2.1 OQ-P1-01 ('v_ace_batch_status is a Section B view, so freshness (A2.14) and every job that starts on the ACE batch record depend on it') and A2.14 OQ-P1-02 ('Freshness before RWB-ACE-001 lands. The register costs a fallback of Tier 1 views plus the case list, but names no freshness source for it'); TSD P1 v3 T3.7 ('Before Section B | v_ace_batch_status does not exist until RWB-ACE-001 lands. Until then every source-fed product shows STALE with no business date, and no data job starts on its own') and T3.2; FSD P1 v3 A2.14 BR-P1-014-2 ('Freshness is read from v_ace_batch_status only. The Workbench never infers it from a row count, a file or a view's data_as_of') and BR-P1-014-4 ('No data job for a business date starts until the ALS batch for that date is COMPLETED')
area: Gate: behaviour before the Section B batch view exists, and the status of a refusal
owner_role: Recovery tech lead with the ACE team lead and the platform team that owns the RWB-ACE-001 sequence
proposed: While v_ace_batch_status does not exist, the read answers exactly as it does for an incomplete batch: 409 with MSG-P1-001, no candidate and no break row, and DP01 is never stamped LOADED for the date, so the case creation job creates no case for that date. The gate is read from the view only and is never inferred from data_as_of, a row count or a file, so no fallback is invented. The refusal status 409 and the two filled fields of MSG-P1-001 are fixed in the published contract and settled in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-4.

title: The shape and the home of the REC-05 break list are not specified, and the table that held it leaves the schema
source: FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.11 (REC-05, OQ-P1-06), A2.12; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result) and T3.9; Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 5 X9 and section 7 AC13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R9
section: 4 Flow step 9; 5 Exception paths X3; 7 Acceptance criteria AC5; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.8; 13 Solution plan build step 6
description: Four things about the listing are unresolved. (1) No source gives a field list for a break row: the legacy dq_exception table leaves the schema, dq_rule leaves with it, and FSD OQ-P1-06 states that 'reconciliation_result holds only the totals. Where the per-account break list is kept needs a decision'. (2) No source says which side of the check a key belongs to when the key is read from an ACE view rather than from a Workbench table: REC-05 is defined over 'every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code on a Workbench table', while the keys this read meets come from v_ace_ca_relation. (3) No source names the view a missing key belongs to, the key types a break may carry, or whether a break is one row per key or one row per key and check. (4) No source says who reads the list and where: the FSD says the data steward and, where the row is missing in ACE, the ACE team, but names no operation and no screen for it, and RWB-P1-E1011-APP keeps the reconciliation job, whose own open point this is.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.11 OQ-P1-06 ('The reconciliation break rows were written to dq_exception, which leaves the schema. reconciliation_result holds only the totals. Where the per-account break list is kept needs a decision'), A2.11.2 ('REC-05 | v_ace_account, v_ace_customer, v_ace_asset and v_ace_payment | Every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code on a Workbench table | Business key, count and amount | Zero orphans; every one listed'), BR-P1-011-3 ('A REC-05 orphan never deletes or changes a Workbench record; it is listed for the data steward and, where the row is missing in ACE, for the ACE team') and AC-ALT-P1-011-03 ('the REC-05 result is BREAK with 1 orphan And "case_party.person_key P0099881" is on the break list for the data steward and the ACE team'); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result fields DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129, totals only) and T3.9 ('REC-05 | Every business key on a Workbench row resolves in its view ... The matching v_ace_* view; replaces the foreign key the boundary rule forbids'); legacy RWB-E1-018 section 5 X9 and section 7 AC13
area: Reconciliation: the REC-05 break row, its key types and its home
owner_role: Data architect with the data steward and the P1 owner of the reconciliation job
proposed: Return the breaks in the same response as the candidates: one row per key and view that has no row, with keyType ACCOUNT or PERSON, businessKey, viewName and businessDate, listed for the data steward and the ACE team, and counted in the run log of the call. No table is created for them and no dq_ table returns; the durable list stays with RWB-P1-E1011-APP, which owns the reconciliation and the OQ-P1-06 decision. Settled in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-5 and proved in AC5.

title: The product group of a candidate row: whether the ACE product_category value is passed through or mapped to the LOV-PRODUCT codes, and what happens to a value outside the list, is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-018 sections 3, 7 (AC1, AC12) and 11; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.2 and A2.18; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.3, T3.4 and T3.8; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 (REQ-CWC-003); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and R9
section: 4 Flow step 5; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1; 8 Business rules BR7; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story groups accounts by 'the product group read from v_ace_account.product_category' and its criteria use the values MORTGAGE and HIRE_PURCHASE, which are also two of the four values of LOV-PRODUCT (MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED). No source states the relation between an ACE product_category value and a LOV-PRODUCT code: whether the view value is already the list code, whether a mapping or a reference load converts one to the other, what happens when an ACE category has no list value (a fifth category, or NULL), or whether a candidate with an unmapped category is returned at all. The FSD's case list and its reconciliation are keyed by product group as a list value, so the question changes a count if it is answered differently on the two sides.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 4 step 8 ('groups the remaining accounts by the borrower person_key and the product group read from v_ace_account.product_category'), section 7 AC1 ('product_category "HIRE_PURCHASE"') and AC12 ('one with product group "MORTGAGE" and one with "HIRE_PURCHASE"'), and section 11 (DF-ACE-010 v_ace_account.product_category); TSD P1 v3 T3.4 ('DF-ACE-010 | product_category | TEXT | varchar(255) | No | None | ACE product.product_category'), T3.8 ('LOV-PRODUCT | MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME, UNSECURED') and T3.3 (v_ace_product carries product_category and product_category_efs); FSD P1 v3 A2.18 ('product_group | Product group (DF-RPT-007) | varchar(15) | Yes | LOV-PRODUCT'); Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 REQ-CWC-003 ('One case covers one customer and one product')
area: Product group: pass-through or mapping to LOV-PRODUCT, and the unmapped value
owner_role: Business analyst, P1 with the center of excellence and the owner of the rwb-case reference data
proposed: Return product_group as the product_category value the view returned, unvalidated and unmapped, so this read holds no list and no mapping table; a value outside LOV-PRODUCT is returned as read and is never coerced, dropped or defaulted. Any mapping, label or validation is the consumer's, through the rwb-case reference-data contract, where the list and its versions live. Settled in ASM-B-P1-07-E1018-6 and proved in AC1 with the two legacy values.

The API Specification and TSD P1 appendix T-A carry the DP07 read as API-P1-010 GET /data-products/{productCode}/records on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, and the contract of this key (RWB-P6-E1055-CON section 12.2) consumes it as /data-products/DP07/records; no source names a /proof-of-delivery resource, and the legacy story names no path at all because the read was an in-process method RecoveryDataApi.proofOfDelivery(LocalDate). source: Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 8 ('writes the delivery to the interaction ledger') and section 11 (DF-INT-002 case_id, DF-INT-004 occurred_at, DF-INT-011 summary written through the ledger writer) with section 10 (SY-DATALOAD runs the read); RWB-P6-E1055-CON section 12.2 (POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions, 'the outbound LETTER entry') and section 19; RWB-P6-E1055-APP sections 4 step 7, 12.2 and 12.8; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.6 and the ledger columns; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.2 DP05 row (interaction is a Workbench table); Ownership Map v1 (interaction owner P1, ruling 'ledger and intake rule stay with P1 rwb-source-data'); Template and Rules v1 Â§R3 default ruling and Â§R5.5 DP-18
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow steps 7 and 8; 5 Exception paths X4; 7 Acceptance criteria AC3 and AC4; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 13 Components and Configuration
description: The delivery entry is a fact with three possible authors and no source picks one. (1) The legacy story writes it inside rwb-comms (section 4 step 8), where the notice and therefore the case are known. (2) The contract and the app story of rwb-comms keep that reading: rwb-comms writes 'the delivery entry on delivery' through POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions. (3) The work package of this key gives the write to rwb-source-data as part of the source read. The second half is the case. The ledger requires a case on every entry (REQ-ILG-002; the writer of RWB-P1-E1066-APP refuses an append without one), while a v_ace_pod row carries pod_key, account_key, notice_ref and the dates and no case at all; the account-to-case link is rwb-case's and is not a dependency of this story (C is RWB-P6-E1055-CON only). So a write here needs the case from the caller, and no source says the caller names it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 4 step 8 and section 11 ('DF-INT-002 interaction case_id - Write, through the ledger writer'); RWB-P6-E1055-CON section 12.2 row 3 ('POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions ... The outbound LETTER entry') and RWB-P6-E1055-APP section 4 step 7 ('rwb-comms writes the outbound LETTER entry through the interaction operation of rwb-source-data'); TSD P1 v3 T3.3 row 24 (v_ace_pod keyed on pod_key and account_key; no case column); RWB-P1-E1066-APP sections 7 AC5 to AC7 and 12.1 (the append requires a case and answers 404 for an unknown one)
proposed: Let this story write the delivery entry through the ledger writer of this service, inside the same transaction as the read, for the case the caller names on the read (caseId), and let rwb-comms write only the dispatch entry; a read without caseId writes nothing. If the contract freeze keeps the write with rwb-comms, this story answers the rows only and AC3 and AC4 move to RWB-P6-E1055-APP.
